before.label: History of science
before.description: Studies scientific knowledge, practices, instruments, institutions, and their historical settings. Histories of ideas, social and cultural histories, and material approaches coexist. The field predates Kuhn and STS, which transform parts of its questions without founding or exhausting it.
before.representative_figures_and_works: George Sarton; Alexandre Koyré, Études galiléennes (1939); Robert K. Merton; Thomas Kuhn, The Structure of Scientific Revolutions (1962); Steven Shapin and Simon Schaffer, Leviathan and the Air-Pump (1985). before.label: African history: postwar institutional expansion
before.date_label: Older traditions · Ibadan · Dar es Salaam · 1950s–
before.description: Postwar institutions challenge colonial denials of African historical agency while building on older African historical knowledge and writing. Oral traditions, documentary criticism, archaeology, and linguistics support diverse inquiries. Nationalist, Marxist, social, and cultural projects overlap and contend; their institutional expansion is not the beginning of African historical thought.

before.scope_note: The node concerns postwar institutions, not the beginning of African historical knowledge. Nationalist, Marxist, oral, and other methods require distinct contexts. Ibadan, Dar es Salaam and UNESCO are distinct institutional settings. Earlier Yoruba writing, West African spoken knowledge, East African reconstruction, women’s histories and labor inquiry are not one nationalist programme. Northern Africa and further African intellectual traditions still require expansion.
